dossier.architecture: Over-bumper collector, selectable note paths, low shooting pivot and elevator for amp/trap.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; package balances wide acquisition with alternate scoring paths.
subsystems.intake: Full-width deployed intake, with replaceable side assemblies and printed funnel blocks.
subsystems.transfer: Two beam breaks track the note; staging leaves the choice between shooter and amp path open.
subsystems.scoring: Pivoted flywheel shooter; elevated alternate path handles amp/trap notes.
subsystems.endgame: Elevator presents the trap note; full hanger details need separate verification.
subsystems.controls: Two cameras/two Orange Pis, odometry-error fusion, shooting-on-move autonomous and missed-note fallback.

versions: Quick five-note alpha; unsuccessful three-pivot beta; final simpler architecture. After first event, bent intake plates led to compliant polycarbonate/5052 construction.
dossier.analysis: Late binding of the scoring destination reduces coordination failures when a partner changes plans. The rebuild history also shows why early autonomous success does not validate every later architectural addition.
limits: Configuration description is tied to the cited interview; not a claim that every unreported shop revision is known.

context_documents.title: 2024-1678 · Staging before selecting a scorer preserves tactical optionality
context_documents.body:
# 2024-1678: Staging before selecting a scorer preserves tactical optionality

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The collector changed from relatively rigid plates to more flexible material after early bending, with replaceable side assemblies. Two beam breaks track staging before the robot chooses the main shooter or elevated amp/trap path. The team describes an early simple robot, a problematic multi-arm beta and the final architecture.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team connects flexible plates to surviving contact and says the intermediate architecture did not work well. Retaining a staged note before selecting its destination is an explicit feature of the final flow.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The branch point in a transfer path is a strategic decision. Delaying the destination choice lets the alliance respond to amplification, traffic or a blocked route without reacquiring the piece. The cost is an extra controlled state that must keep the note centered and releasable. Historical version labels should not collapse the failed beta into the final competition mechanism.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test repeated stage-and-wait cycles, destination changes after acquisition and jam recovery at the branch. Evaluate repair time for a damaged collector side as well as pickup speed.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/wmNuuUsm9GY](https://youtu.be/wmNuuUsm9GY)

source_reviews.title: Nik public Superstructure.java
source_reviews.locator: Beam-break declarations, updateShootingSetpoints, intakeToHoldTransition, fireState and elevator transitions
facts: The release declares separate serializer, feeder and amp beam breaks. Feeder detection triggers intake clearing and stops the serializer in the hold sequence.
Fire waits on the shooter request then feeds until the feeder beam clears. Amp extension waits on the amp beam and uses a motion plan.
Speaker targeting passes measured chassis velocity to its shooting solution. The published command uses the same setpoint on both shooter outputs in the reviewed method.
source_reviews.limitations: Code on main is not pinned to an event. A declared sensor does not authenticate all physical installations.

source_reviews.title: Citrus Circuits 2024 public robot code
facts: Team calls the 2024 robot Nik. A request system coordinates intake, index rollers and elevator. The motion planner is intended to avoid intake/elevator interference.
source_reviews.limitations: The older corpus uses Epsilon. No source reviewed here establishes its scope as a separate version name.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Nik combines a deployed intake, chassis-aimed variable-angle shooting and a distinct elevated placement route. The public software makes the coordination visible. Different beam breaks identify a note at the serializer, feeder or amp stage. Once the feeder sees a note, separate requests clear the intake and stop the transfer. The elevator is a second destination, with software ordering to make space around the deployed collector. Together these details explain why this machine can share volume without assuming every mechanism can move simultaneously.
piece_flow: Older corpus describes a full-width over-bumper collector and guides into the serializer. The code starts the pickup and serializer while the feeder is idle.
Feeder beam interruption causes the serializer to idle and the intake to clear and tuck. The note can wait short of the shooter.
Fire waits for the shooter, runs the serializer/feeder and watches for feeder clearance. The alternate placement route uses amp beam confirmation before extension and during release.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The vertical scorer and deployed intake overlap enough that motion order matters. In the amp score transition, intake clearance precedes elevator retraction and final intake tuck. That is a geometric constraint expressed as a sequence. If the robot loses its reference on one axis, simply replaying the nominal sequence may be insufficient. Draw safe escape directions at each state, including a note trapped at the boundary.

subsystems.name: Deployed intake and staging
subsystems.construction: Inherited over-bumper collector, centering blocks and replaceable side assemblies. Code confirms deploy actuator, serializer, feeder and three declared beam breaks.
subsystems.operation: Acquire until feeder occupancy, then clear and tuck the collector and stop the path.
subsystems.team_rationale: Published controls distinguish a note held for a shot from one in the elevator.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Sensor distinctions let the drive team or state machine recover based on where the note actually is. A clear beam through the open center of a ring does not necessarily mean empty unless sensor placement and timing support that interpretation.
subsystems.interfaces: Intake clearance, feeder datum and sensor threshold need to stay valid when the rollers or funnel are serviced.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Exercise partial capture, skewed notes and failure to clear a beam. Inspect whether an operator can interrupt and recover without losing a held note.
subsystems.unknowns: Physical sensor brackets, false readings and event-installed versions.

subsystems.name: Elevator and amp rollers
subsystems.construction: Separate elevator, roller stage and amp beam break are visible in the code.
subsystems.operation: Verify occupancy, move using a clearance plan, release and order the return motions.
subsystems.team_rationale: README identifies avoiding contact between the elevator and intake as the planner's purpose.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A short commanded path is only safe if it lies inside a clearance region with backlash, flex and sensor drift included. A timed recovery on one axis may need a slower or mechanically bounded route.
subsystems.interfaces: Overlap of intake, elevator, held note and stowed chassis envelope.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test start from an interrupted state and replace one damaged intake side, then rerun the clearance check.
subsystems.unknowns: Geometric margins, state timeouts outside reviewed methods and trap success.

subsystems.name: Speaker aim and feed readiness
subsystems.construction: Code computes heading, hood and shooter setpoints from field pose and passes measured velocity for speaker targeting.
subsystems.operation: Coordinate chassis heading and release after shooter readiness.
subsystems.team_rationale: README describes a heading override during auto-align and separate shooting/ferry maps.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Motion compensation should be validated by shot residual versus chassis velocity and pose age. A drive-induced error can look like a hood calibration error.
subsystems.interfaces: Pose timestamps, hood position, wheel readiness and feeder edge timing.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Log all four during moving shots and after localization loss.
subsystems.unknowns: Actual tuned map range, camera occlusion and hit rates by pose.

revisions: Team release names Nik. The older dossier name and hardware history remain distinct from the source revision studied here.
transferable_principles: Model collision-safe motion ordering explicitly. Use distinct sensing for a captured note, a ready feed and a loaded secondary scorer.
disconfirming_conditions: A shared envelope is a poor transfer if damage or lost reference leaves no safe recovery path. Moving shots lose value when localization age or heading lag exceeds the release tolerance.
remaining_gaps: Event-pinned code, primary mechanical assembly sections, caption review and logged shot outcomes.
recommended_images: Side elevation showing intake clearance poses and amp travel
Feeder and amp beam locations with a note present
